On Floreana, the history of islanders sits alongside the lives of seabirds and other animals. One of the inhabited Galápagos Islands, it has the small settlement of Puerto Velasco Ibarra, green uplands, and open ocean along its shores. Visitors come for walks along nature trails and stories of sailors, settlers, and the first attempts to make a life on volcanic land.

At Punta Cormorant, the sand comes in two distinct shades: one beach is greenish because of olivine, while another is pale and mixed with coral particles. A path leads to a lagoon where flamingos can be observed. Pink silhouettes in the shallows, dark lava, and turquoise ocean offer so many photographic scenes that it is tempting to make the walk last longer. Sea lions and birds are best watched quietly, leaving them plenty of space.

In Post Office Bay, the tradition of a postal barrel installed by whalers back in 1793 survives. Travelers leave postcards and pick up others if they can deliver them to the addressees. Writing a few lines by hand is especially enjoyable here: each small message continues the island's maritime history.

Further inland, Floreana becomes greener. The Asilo de la Paz area introduces the settlers' past, while the coast draws attention back to wildlife. Visits to individual areas and boat outings depend on the chosen itinerary: the island can be explored through a mix of walks, wildlife encounters, and a short immersion in its human history.

Florianópolis is located on Santa Catarina Island and is connected to the mainland. Its ocean coastline, lagoons, dunes, and urban neighborhoods make it possible to alternate beach time, walks, and outings around the island.

The beaches are the main attraction. There are many of them, and the Atlantic waves make Florianópolis a well-known surfing destination. A separate day can be spent around Conceição Lagoon.

Several days by the coast can be complemented by the historic center, museums, and a visit to the market. Florianópolis combines well with other destinations in southern Brazil, especially Curitiba and Porto Alegre.

Fortaleza Canyon lies in Serra Geral National Park in southern Brazil, near Cambará do Sul. Its scenery unfolds in a vast panorama: long rock walls frame green valleys, and the edge of a grassy plateau offers views into the depth of the gorge.

Walks along the upper part of the canyon reveal the scale of the landscape from different vantage points. Clouds and fog can obscure distant slopes, so visibility can change even during a single visit. Fortaleza complements the nearby Itaimbezinho Canyon with more open views and suits a nature itinerary through southern Brazil. It is a separate natural landmark, unrelated to the city of the same name on Brazil's northeastern coast.

Fortaleza is on Brazil's northeastern coast and is the capital of Ceará state. The city is associated with the Atlantic Ocean, beaches, dunes, and the historic fort from which it takes its name.

The beach areas include Iracema, Meireles, Mucuripe, and Cumbuco. More active days can feature surfing, diving, boat excursions, and buggy trips over the dunes.

Fortaleza can be a standalone coastal stop or part of a longer route through northeastern Brazil, combining the city's attractions with the sea and natural landscapes.
